intro: Cards, board games, bets and nights out: the vocabulary of play.
p.tocarle a alguien.nota: Me toca a mí: it's my turn.
b1.texto:
**Three words for game.** **Un juego** is the game as such: el ajedrez es **un juego**. **Una partida** is one game of cards, chess or a video game: **echar una partida**. **Un partido** is a match in sport: **un partido** de tenis.

**Cards.** **La baraja española** has forty cards and four suits: **oros**, **copas**, **espadas** and **bastos**. You **barajas**, you **repartes**, you **echas** una carta. The most Spanish game is **el mus**.

**Board games.** On **el tablero** you move **las fichas** after you **tiras el dado**. **El ajedrez**, **las damas**, **el parchís**.

**Turns.** The verb is **tocar**, built like gustar: **¿A quién le toca?** **Me toca a mí.** **Te toca tirar.**

**Tocar** also means to win by luck: **le ha tocado la lotería**; **me tocó** un viaje en un sorteo.

**Rules.** **Seguir las reglas**, **saltarse las reglas**, **hacer trampas**. **Jugar limpio** or **sucio**. **¡Eso no vale!** (that doesn't count!)

**Chance.** **Los juegos de azar**: **la lotería**, **la quiniela** (football pools), **las apuestas**. **Apostar** dinero: **te apuesto** diez euros **a que** gana.

**Children.** **Jugar al escondite** (hide and seek), **a la comba** (skipping), **a las canicas** (marbles); **el columpio** and **el tobogán**.

**Fun.** **Un pasatiempo**; **pasar el rato**; **entretenerse**. **Salir de juerga**, **irse de fiesta**. **Disfrazarse de** pirata for **una fiesta de disfraces**. **Pasárselo en grande.** And at the end of the town festival, **los fuegos artificiales**.
b2.titulo: A game of cards after dinner
b2.f0: Come on, shall we have a game? You shuffle, Daniel, and I'll deal.
b2.f1: OK, but this time no cheating, Grandma, I know you.
b2.f2: I never cheat! The thing is, I'm lucky. Whose turn is it?
b2.f3: It's my turn. I bet you a euro that I win this one.
b2.f4: Done. But looking at my cards in the mirror doesn't count, eh?
b2.f5: If you hadn't hidden a card up your sleeve on Sunday, nobody would distrust you.
b4.o0.refuerzo: One game of cards or chess.
b5.pregunta: Complete: it's your turn to throw.
b5.o0.refuerzo: Tocarle a alguien: to be someone's turn.
b5.o1.refuerzo: The verb stays in the third person, like gustar.
b5.o2.refuerzo: The verb for turns is tocar.
b6.pregunta: Le ha tocado la lotería means…
b6.o2.refuerzo: With a prize, tocar means to win.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I bet you that he comes.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The verb needs a: apostar a que.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The verb needs a: apostar a que.
b8.o0: He dressed up as a pirate.
b8.o1.explicacion: Disfrazarse de: to dress up as.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Barajar means to shuffle, the step before dealing the cards.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Apostar means to bet, which is not the step you take before dealing.
b10.traduccion: We had a great time at the fancy-dress party.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write the complete rules of a game you know well, so that someone could play it without ever having seen it.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Give your opinion aloud on gambling and online betting among young people.
b8.o0.explicacion: Se disfrazó de means he dressed up as, using a costume.
